lessons.name: Humanoid
lessons.summary: Humanoid builds industrial humanoid robots and the software that coordinates their work and teaches them new skills.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Humanoid builds industrial humanoid robots and the software that coordinates their work and teaches them new skills.

![HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled with a human-shaped upper body on a wheeled base](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-humanoid.webp)
*HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled with a human-shaped upper body on a wheeled base. Source: [Site](https://thehumanoid.ai), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **HMND 01 Alpha** has a human-shaped upper body; the wheeled version moves through industrial spaces without needing to balance on legs.
- **KinetIQ** coordinates robot fleets, while KinetIQ Ascend develops manipulation skills through reinforcement learning: improving actions using feedback from trial and error.
- **Published specifications** for Alpha Wheeled include a 15 kg payload and up to four hours of runtime; these are manufacturer figures, not student measurements.

> **Key idea:** A humanoid product combines useful hands, reliable movement, and fleet software; human shape alone does not make it useful.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an orchestration service:** KinetIQ connects high-level assignments to individual robot actions, rather than treating every joint as a separate application.
- **Follow HMND 01 Alpha and KinetIQ** together in the map: hardware capability and the software deciding what happens next are different learning targets.
- **Worked reading exercise:** for a four-hour demonstration shift, list charging, recovery, and task-change time separately; a runtime claim does not establish productive uptime.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the company-linked interview**, then inspect the wheeled product page to distinguish demonstrated tasks from future ambitions.
2. **Read the technology articles** and sketch which layer assigns work, learns skills, and executes motions.
3. **Use the public enquiry channel** for one focused technical question about task recovery; do not assume robot loans or external access.

lessons.name: Hydromea
lessons.summary: Hydromea builds underwater inspection robots, wireless optical communications, and propulsion systems for collecting data below the surface.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Hydromea builds underwater inspection robots, wireless optical communications, and propulsion systems for collecting data below the surface.

![EXRAY underwater inspection robot in Hydromea’s product imagery](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-hydromea.webp)
*EXRAY underwater inspection robot in Hydromea’s product imagery. Source: [Site](https://www.hydromea.com/exray-underwater-robot), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **EXRAY** is a compact inspection robot for submerged structures, including confined tanks; its modular connections accept different sensing payloads.
- **LUMA** sends data through water using light, while DISKDRIVE provides propulsion: the force that moves the robot.
- **NAVIA** is the operator interface; NAVIA+ organizes inspection findings into reports with points of interest linked to their locations.

> **Key idea:** Underwater inspection is a data-delivery problem as well as a robot-movement problem.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a remote debugging session:** a useful robot must return observations that an operator can interpret, not merely reach an interesting place.
- **EXRAY connects hardware to evidence:** cameras, navigation, communication, and reporting all contribute to the final inspection record.
- **Worked example:** compare a visual defect image with a thickness measurement from an ultrasound payload; they answer different maintenance questions, even at the same location.

## How to engage

1. **Watch LUMA in use**, then compare the communication page with the EXRAY product description.
2. **Make a mission checklist:** target surface, required measurement, visibility, communication path, and the report an inspector needs.
3. **Contact Hydromea publicly** about an educational inspection-data talk; propose an offline analysis exercise rather than access to a tank or industrial asset.

lessons.name: Inbolt
lessons.summary: Inbolt adds vision and AI guidance to industrial robots so they can adapt their motions to the parts in front of them.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Inbolt adds vision and AI guidance to industrial robots so they can adapt their motions to the parts in front of them.

![Inbolt vision equipment mounted beside an industrial robot work area](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-inbolt.webp)
*Inbolt vision equipment mounted beside an industrial robot work area. Source: [Site](https://www.inbolt.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The Inbolt Platform** combines robot programming, a vision model, and robot control rather than manufacturing a replacement industrial arm.
- **Robot Control** connects vision guidance to controllers from FANUC, Universal Robots, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa, and Comau.
- **The physical problem** is variation: parts do not always arrive in precisely the position expected by a fixed robot program.

> **Key idea:** Seeing the current part position can be more useful than making every part arrive at exactly the same position.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of runtime input validation:** instead of trusting an assumed object location, vision supplies evidence before the motion is executed.
- **Inbolt GuideNOW** is the related map node; use the current platform pages to understand today’s product terminology rather than assuming names never change.
- **Worked example:** study a de-racking demonstration and identify the observed part, its position estimate, and the arm correction; separate perception failure from motion failure.

## How to engage

1. **Start with the platform demonstrations** and choose one use case, such as bin picking or fastening.
2. **Read the controller integration page** and write down what remains the responsibility of the existing robot controller.
3. **Send a public technical enquiry** with a small vision experiment and one question about measuring pose errors, not a generic sponsorship request.

lessons.name: iniVation
lessons.summary: iniVation builds event-based vision systems that report changing pixels instead of only sending complete camera frames.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

iniVation builds event-based vision systems that report changing pixels instead of only sending complete camera frames.

![iniVation event-vision camera hardware](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-inivation.webp)
*iniVation event-vision camera hardware. Source: [Site](https://www.inivation.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Dynamic Vision Sensor**, or DVS, reports individual pixel-level brightness changes with microsecond time resolution.
- **Event vision** resembles an event stream in software: transmit changes when they happen rather than repeatedly polling an entire image.
- **Aeveon** extends this approach with multiple event types and full-frame readout; do not assume every iniVation device has identical outputs.

> **Key idea:** The representation arriving from a sensor shapes both the algorithms and the debugging tools you need.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **A different perception input** makes iniVation useful for students comparing conventional images with fast, change-driven measurements.
- **Worked example:** watch a moving object against a still background; ask which pixels produce changes and why a static scene provides different information.
- **Start with the data format:** a stream of pixel coordinates, times, and changes is not directly interchangeable with a standard image tensor.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official introduction** before browsing the application videos; separate the sensing principle from any particular robot demonstration.
2. **Read the technology and solutions pages** and choose one use case where timing matters more than ordinary color imagery.
3. **Use the public developer material** to frame a question about recording and replaying data; request sample data before considering hardware.

lessons.name: ISYBOT
lessons.summary: ISYBOT makes collaborative industrial robots that help operators perform sanding, grinding, and surface-finishing tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ISYBOT makes collaborative industrial robots that help operators perform sanding, grinding, and surface-finishing tasks.

![ISYBOT arm holding a finishing tool against an industrial workpiece](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-isybot.webp)
*ISYBOT arm holding a finishing tool against an industrial workpiece. Source: [Site](https://isybot.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A cobot**, short for collaborative robot, is designed for work involving people; the specific task still determines the safety measures needed.
- **The SYB 3** has three controlled axes, a 1.6 m working radius, and a stated 10 kg payload throughout its working area.
- **Four operating modes** include assistance, replay, parallel work, and teleoperation: controlling the machine from a distance.

> **Key idea:** For finishing work, controlling contact with the surface matters as much as following a geometric path.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of recording a macro:** an operator teaches a useful movement, then the robot repeats it with process settings such as applied pressure.
- **ISYBOT sanding cobot** is the connected map node; inspect the tool and work surface, not only the shape of the arm.
- **Worked example:** compare sanding a flat panel with a curved train body; list where contact direction and pressure must change despite a similar overall movement.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official application video**, noting how the machine is positioned and how the operator works around it.
2. **Read the solutions page** and draw the difference between assistance and replay modes.
3. **Ask through the public contact channel** for an educational process-control discussion; suggest analysis of demonstration footage rather than operating an industrial sanding tool.

lessons.name: Jaipur Robotics
lessons.summary: Jaipur Robotics uses computer vision and automation software to help waste-to-energy plants understand and handle incoming waste.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Jaipur Robotics uses computer vision and automation software to help waste-to-energy plants understand and handle incoming waste.

![Waste-handling crane shown on Jaipur Robotics’ product page](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-jaipur-robotics.webp)
*Waste-handling crane shown on Jaipur Robotics’ product page. Source: [Site](https://jaipurrobotics.com/products), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Waste-to-energy plants** burn waste to produce usable energy; Jaipur focuses on information needed to manage the waste before combustion.
- **Its products** detect oversized or dangerous items, map calorific value, and track cranes moving waste through the plant.
- **Calorific value** means the energy obtainable from burning material; mapping it supports decisions about mixing different waste loads.

> **Key idea:** An industrial robotics company may improve perception and operations without selling a general-purpose robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of observability for a physical service:** cameras and analytics help operators notice problematic inputs before they disrupt downstream equipment.
- **A concrete software entry point** is object detection, meaning locating and classifying items in images, rather than building a new crane.
- **Worked example:** distinguish an oversized-object alert from a crane-location trace; one describes a hazard in the waste, the other describes equipment movement.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official homepage footage**, then read the product descriptions to identify where each observation is collected.
2. **Make a mock event schema:** record image time, detected item, confidence, and operator decision using invented test data clearly labeled as synthetic.
3. **Contact the company through its public form** about an offline industrial-vision discussion; do not assume access to plant imagery or operational machinery.

lessons.name: Japet Medical
lessons.summary: Japet Medical develops and integrates wearable assistance devices, including the motorized Japet.W+ back-support exoskeleton.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Japet Medical develops and integrates wearable assistance devices, including the motorized Japet.W+ back-support exoskeleton.

![Workers using Japet back-support exoskeletons](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-japet-medical.webp)
*Workers using Japet back-support exoskeletons. Source: [Site](https://www.japet.eu/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **An exoskeleton** is a device worn outside the body to assist movement or posture; it is not necessarily a powered robot.
- **Japet.W+** is described as motorized lumbar support: it assists the lower back while allowing the wearer to move.
- **The wider range** includes devices for shoulders, neck, and posture; Japet also assesses tasks and supports workplace integration.

> **Key idea:** A wearable robot must fit the person and the task, not just produce an impressive mechanical motion.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an adaptive interface:** assistance should follow the user’s movement rather than force every user through the same scripted sequence.
- **The Japet.W+ map node** makes human–machine interaction concrete: comfort, movement, and use conditions belong in the engineering discussion.
- **Worked example:** compare carrying an object with working overhead; these load different body regions, so one assistance device cannot automatically answer both needs.

## How to engage

1. **Read the Japet.W+ page** and compare it with the shoulder-support device; identify which product is explicitly motorized.
2. **Map one fictional workstation** into movement, duration, body region, and evaluation questions; do not treat marketing benefits as your own measured medical outcomes.
3. **Use Japet’s public contact channel** to request an educational ergonomics discussion, not personal medical advice or an unsupervised device trial.

lessons.name: Kompaï Robotics
lessons.summary: Kompaï Robotics develops mobile robots for assistance, logistics, and research, adapting platforms to the place where they will work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Kompaï Robotics develops mobile robots for assistance, logistics, and research, adapting platforms to the place where they will work.

![Kompaï mobile assistance robot beside a person](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-kompai-robotics.webp)
*Kompaï mobile assistance robot beside a person. Source: [Site](https://www.kompai.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **An autonomous mobile robot**, or AMR, travels to a requested destination while detecting and avoiding obstacles.
- **Kompaï’s applications** include transporting equipment between departments and supporting interaction in care environments.
- **Research platforms** offer tailored APIs: application programming interfaces through which software can request or observe robot functions.

> **Key idea:** A mobile base becomes useful when navigation is connected to a real workflow and a clear human interface.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a delivery API:** requesting a destination is different from implementing the navigation that makes the delivery happen.
- **The logistics courier example** has four independent drive wheels and a stated 250 kg payload; that is a specific platform, not every Kompaï robot.
- **Worked example:** break a hospital equipment delivery into request, travel, handover, and confirmation; decide which events a student dashboard should display.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the homepage-linked robot video**, then compare the robot catalogue with the logistics courier page.
2. **Design a simulated delivery dashboard** that distinguishes a completed journey from a confirmed handover; keep this separate from a claim of real integration.
3. **Ask through the official contact channel** about API documentation or an educational talk; an open API does not establish an open-source license.

lessons.name: Kyber
lessons.summary: Kyber builds low-latency streaming infrastructure for remotely observing and controlling machines, including robots.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Kyber builds low-latency streaming infrastructure for remotely observing and controlling machines, including robots.

![Kyber’s published connection architecture diagram](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-kyber.webp)
*Kyber’s published connection architecture diagram. Source: [Site](https://kyber.tech/technology), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Teleoperation** means a person controls a robot remotely; the operator needs current video and the robot needs timely commands.
- **Kyber synchronizes** video, audio, control inputs, and sensor measurements onto one timeline, rather than leaving each stream on an independent clock.
- **The company describes** training-data collection, monitoring, and human takeover as robotics uses; its main product has an AGPL open-source licensing option.

> **Key idea:** A fast connection is not enough: the image, action, and sensor reading must also refer to the same moment.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of distributed tracing:** timestamps make observations from separate processes interpretable as one physical interaction.
- **Kyber teleoperation stack** is the related map node; it is infrastructure for an operator loop, not a robot policy that learns the task itself.
- **Worked example:** pair a camera frame with a gripper-close command and a contact reading; ask how clock drift could produce the wrong training label.

## How to engage

1. **Try the technology page’s latency comparison** and inspect its streaming demonstration before reading architecture claims.
2. **Read the robotics page** and sketch what should happen if the link degrades; do not equate a best-case latency claim with your network.
3. **Inspect the public repository and license** before integration, then report reproducible network conditions when asking the community a technical question.

lessons.name: Leju Robotics
lessons.summary: Leju Robotics builds the KUAVO humanoid family and provides platforms and community resources for embodied-AI development.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Leju Robotics builds the KUAVO humanoid family and provides platforms and community resources for embodied-AI development.

![Leju KUAVO humanoid shown on the maker’s homepage](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-leju-robotics.webp)
*Leju KUAVO humanoid shown on the maker’s homepage. Source: [Site](https://www.lejurobot.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A humanoid** uses a roughly human-shaped body; Leju’s product range includes KUAVO 4Pro and KUAVO 5 / 5-W.
- **Its application pages** distinguish research, business services, industrial work, and training environments rather than presenting one universal deployment.
- **OpenLET** is presented as a developer community connecting real-robot data, development tools, documentation, and technical exchange.

> **Key idea:** A research platform is valuable when students can understand the tools and data around the robot, not merely watch it move.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a hardware development platform:** the body provides capabilities, while software experiments determine which tasks become reproducible.
- **Leju KUAVO** is the connected map node; compare the exact robot variant in footage before transferring claims between models.
- **Worked example:** contrast exhibition guidance with factory manipulation; list the input data, physical actions, and failure conditions each application would need.

## How to engage

1. **Start at the official video centre** to see the company’s platforms and distinguish staged motion from interaction with objects.
2. **Read the research and industrial application pages** and write one narrow, testable research question rather than proposing a general humanoid assistant.
3. **Follow the official community links** to inspect available tools and documentation before requesting access; do not assume every advertised resource is openly licensed.

lessons.name: Les Companions
lessons.summary: Les Companions builds PACO, a painting robot that handles repetitive spraying while painters choose and supervise the work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Les Companions builds PACO, a painting robot that handles repetitive spraying while painters choose and supervise the work.

![PACO painting robot working beside a wall](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-les-companions.webp)
*PACO painting robot working beside a wall. Source: [Les Companions](https://www.lescompanions.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **PACO** is a collaborative robot for new buildings and major refurbishments; the painter keeps decision making and detailed finishing work.
- **Scan, program, operate:** the painter measures the room with a three-dimensional scan, defines the painting job, then runs the robot.
- **Airless spraying** pushes paint through a nozzle without compressed air; the company describes controlled paint application and remote progress monitoring.

> **Key idea:** Construction automation starts by translating a changing worksite into a job a machine can repeat.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a compiler:** the room scan is input, the chosen painting job is a program, and robot movement produces the physical output.
- **Worked example:** trace the published scan–program–operate sequence; identify where a doorway must become an excluded region rather than a surface to paint.
- **A useful student connection** is the PACO map node: compare planning around obstacles with controlling a tool near the surface.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the PACO demonstration** and label the human decisions separately from the robot’s repeated motions.
2. **Read the worksite explanation** and sketch a room representation with walls, openings, and paintable surfaces; this is a software exercise.
3. **Use the public demo/contact route** with one question about room geometry or operator corrections, supported by your annotated example.

lessons.name: Lightly
lessons.summary: Lightly builds software for selecting, labeling, evaluating, and training on the visual data used by robots and other camera-based systems.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Lightly builds software for selecting, labeling, evaluating, and training on the visual data used by robots and other camera-based systems.

![LightlyStudio interface for curating an image dataset](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-lightly.webp)
*LightlyStudio interface for curating an image dataset. Source: [Lightly](https://www.lightly.ai/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **LightlyStudio** is the data hub: teams explore images, select useful subsets, annotate objects, and inspect model mistakes.
- **LightlyTrain** handles model training, including self-supervised pretraining: learning visual structure from images before task-specific labels are supplied.
- **An embedding** is a numeric representation of an image or object; Lightly uses these representations for similarity search and sample selection.

> **Key idea:** Better robot perception often begins with choosing better examples, before changing the model architecture.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of test coverage:** thousands of nearly identical camera frames may cover fewer situations than a smaller, deliberately varied collection.
- **Worked example:** collect tabletop images, separate repeated views from unusual lighting, then compare which objects appear in each subset.
- **LightlyStudio and LightlyTrain** are separate map nodes; study how curated data becomes training input and how evaluation informs the next collection.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official interface clips** to connect curation, labeling, and evaluation to visible actions in the tool.
2. **Inspect both public repositories** and their licenses before choosing a local experiment; start with a small dataset you can legally share.
3. **Follow the current training documentation** and report the selected images, held-out evaluation split, and errors when discussing results with the community.

lessons.name: MESH
lessons.summary: MESH develops robotic systems and software that turn digital reinforcement designs into assembled steel cages for concrete construction.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MESH develops robotic systems and software that turn digital reinforcement designs into assembled steel cages for concrete construction.

![MESH robotic fabrication equipment in its production environment](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-mesh.webp)
*MESH robotic fabrication equipment in its production environment. Source: [MESH](https://www.mesh.ch/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Rebar** means reinforcing steel placed inside concrete; a cage is an arrangement of bars joined into the required shape.
- **MESH covers several stages:** production planning, feeding bending machines, joining bars, and assembling the finished cages.
- **Its product families** include PLAN for software, ACTUATE for machine tending, NODE for joining, and ASSEMBLE for handling and assembly.

> **Key idea:** The robot is one part of a manufacturing pipeline that must preserve the designer’s intent through every physical step.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a build system:** the design describes an artifact, dependencies constrain the assembly order, and machines execute the production steps.
- **Worked example:** follow one cage from bar preparation to joining; ask which connections must exist before the unfinished structure can be moved.
- **For a software-first lab,** the interesting bridge is between geometric planning and real materials that can bend, shift, or obstruct a robot.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official fabrication footage** and distinguish bar handling, joining, and human supervision.
2. **Read the ETH Zurich account** alongside the product page; draw an input/output contract for one stage using a small imaginary cage.
3. **Use the public company contact** for a focused planning or digital-fabrication discussion, bringing your process sketch and questions.

lessons.name: Micropsi Industries
lessons.summary: Micropsi Industries builds MIRAI, vision software that teaches industrial robots to adjust movements when production conditions vary.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Micropsi Industries builds MIRAI, vision software that teaches industrial robots to adjust movements when production conditions vary.

![Industrial robot equipped with Micropsi’s MIRAI vision system](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-micropsi-industries.webp)
*Industrial robot equipped with Micropsi’s MIRAI vision system. Source: [Micropsi Industries](https://www.micropsi-industries.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **MIRAI** uses camera observations to guide motion when a part’s position, shape, lighting, or background changes.
- **Training produces a skill:** a mathematical model describing how the robot should move during one action; that skill fits inside a larger robot program.
- **The system combines** robot-control software on a local computing device, a cloud learning service, and a training application.

> **Key idea:** Learning a motion correction does not remove the need to design the surrounding task and its exception handling.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a learned function:** camera observations enter, motion guidance comes out, and the calling program decides when that function should run.
- **Worked example:** study insertion with a shifted part; distinguish finding the opening, correcting the approach, and deciding whether to stop.
- **The MIRAI map node** connects this company to learning from demonstrations; demonstrations show desired behavior rather than spelling out every geometric rule.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official overview** and identify which visible variations the robot handles.
2. **Read the training sequence** and write a small coverage checklist for one tabletop task, varying object location and lighting separately.
3. **Use the public technical enquiry route** to discuss a concrete application and its failure cases; consult current product details before assuming hardware requirements.

lessons.summary: mimic robotics builds learned manipulation systems and robotic hands for industrial tasks involving varied objects, cables, and soft materials.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

mimic robotics builds learned manipulation systems and robotic hands for industrial tasks involving varied objects, cables, and soft materials.

![mimic robotics manipulation demonstration](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-mimic-robotics.webp)
*mimic robotics manipulation demonstration. Source: [mimic robotics](https://www.mimicrobotics.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Dexterity** means skillful object handling; mimic targets assembly, packaging, sorting, and other tasks that require adaptable hand movements.
- **Video-action models** use representations learned from video to help produce robot actions; the company develops FLUX-mimic with Black Forest Labs.
- **Its physical systems** can use one or two arms, on a stationary table or mobile platform, depending on the application.

> **Key idea:** A useful manipulation system must connect what video teaches about motion to the actions a particular hand can execute.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of transfer learning:** a pretrained representation supplies a starting point, then task-specific examples teach the output behavior you actually need.
- **Worked example:** compare handling a cable with picking a rigid box; list the observations needed to notice slipping or a changing object shape.
- **FLUX-mimic** is the connected map node; use it to separate the learned model from the hand, arm, and deployment service.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official task clips** and identify the object, hand contact, and intended result in one assembly sequence.
2. **Read the technology explanation** and note which claims concern learning data and which concern physical hardware.
3. **Approach the public company contact** with an annotated manipulation experiment and one precise question about demonstrations, evaluation, or transfer between robot bodies.

lessons.summary: Mistral AI develops AI models, including Robostral Navigate, which turns camera observations and language instructions into robot navigation decisions.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Mistral AI develops AI models, including Robostral Navigate, which turns camera observations and language instructions into robot navigation decisions.

![Robostral Navigate image published with Mistral’s navigation announcement](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-mistral-ai.webp)
*Robostral Navigate image published with Mistral’s navigation announcement. Source: [Mistral AI](https://mistral.ai/news/robostral-navigate/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Robostral Navigate** accepts images from one RGB camera and an instruction; RGB means the ordinary red, green, and blue color channels.
- **The announced model has eight billion parameters:** these are learned numeric values, not eight billion manually written navigation rules.
- **Mistral describes simulation-based training:** supervised examples teach initial behavior, then reinforcement learning improves it using feedback from attempted tasks.

> **Key idea:** Following a language instruction requires grounding words in observations and repeatedly choosing a useful next movement.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an event loop:** read the camera, update context, choose a movement, then observe again instead of executing a sentence as one fixed script.
- **Worked example:** trace the published instruction from lobby through corridor to a supply-room shelf; mark where a fresh observation changes the next decision.
- **Robostral Navigate** is the related model node; Mistral’s robotics hackathon also provides a concrete connection to Hugging Face (LeRobot).

## How to engage

1. **Watch the navigation demonstration** and distinguish the route instruction from the robot’s individual actions.
2. **Read the announcement** and compare its camera input, simulation training, and evaluation setting before interpreting performance numbers.
3. **Use public event and research channels** to find future activities; the linked hackathon pages describe a past event and its robotics themes.

lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Moon Surgical develops Maestro, a robotic assistance platform that helps surgeons position instruments during minimally invasive surgery.

![Maestro surgical assistance platform shown by Moon Surgical](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-moon-surgical.webp)
*Maestro surgical assistance platform shown by Moon Surgical. Source: [Moon Surgical](https://moonsurgical.com/maestro-system), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Laparoscopy** is surgery through small incisions using long instruments and a camera; Maestro supports the surgeon’s instrument control.
- **The Maestro platform** is designed around the surgeon’s preferred instruments and workflow, with robotic assistance rather than a separately operated console.
- **Maestro Insights** adds software for reviewing operating-room information; this is a distinct layer from moving or holding a physical instrument.

> **Key idea:** A medical robot can be valuable by providing steady, controllable assistance within an existing clinical workflow.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an input device with physical constraints:** user intent must become predictable movement while the interface continuously makes the system’s state understandable.
- **Worked example:** distinguish positioning a camera, holding its view, and reviewing procedure information; these have different inputs and success criteria.
- **The Maestro map node** connects hardware assistance with human–robot interaction; a convincing interface demonstration must explain who controls each action.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official platform clips** to locate the surgeon, robot arms, and instruments in the same scene.
2. **Read the system and Insights pages** and make a responsibility diagram separating user commands, assistance, and information display.
3. **Use the public company channel** to request an educational controls or interface discussion, supported by a nonclinical prototype and a specific question.

MotionLab.Berlin is a hardtech makerspace and innovation community where teams develop physical products using shared workshops, programs, and events.

*MotionLab.Berlin community event inside its workshop venue. Source: [MotionLab.Berlin](https://motionlab.berlin/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Hardtech** means technology that depends on physical engineering as well as software; robot prototypes need both.
- **Shared facilities** include CNC machines, laser cutters, metal workshops, and three-dimensional printing; these turn digital designs into physical parts.
- **The community offers** startup programs, events, and innovation tours, connecting people who build hardware with equipment and practical experience.

> **Key idea:** A robotics ecosystem includes places that help teams build and test machines, as well as companies that sell robots.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of shared infrastructure for hardware:** a workshop provides capabilities a team would otherwise need to purchase, maintain, and learn independently.
- **Worked example:** map a camera-mount project into design, fabrication, fit checking, and revision; mark which stages need tools beyond a laptop.
- **For 42AI,** its public events and tours offer a way to learn how software-focused teams move from a demonstration to a physical prototype.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official space footage** and identify machining, prototyping, and community areas rather than treating the venue as ordinary office space.
2. **Check the current events and tour pages** for formats, access conditions, and dates before planning travel or participation.
3. **Contact the public programs team** with a short project description and specific equipment needs; confirm workshop onboarding and membership terms directly.

lessons.name: Nanoflex Robotics
lessons.summary: Nanoflex Robotics develops magnetic navigation and flexible instruments for remotely assisted procedures inside blood vessels.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Nanoflex Robotics develops magnetic navigation and flexible instruments for remotely assisted procedures inside blood vessels.

![Nanoflex Robotics magnetic navigation technology](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-nanoflex-robotics.webp)
*Nanoflex Robotics magnetic navigation technology. Source: [Nanoflex Robotics](https://nanoflexrobotics.com/our-technology/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Endovascular** means inside blood vessels; the company’s instruments are designed to navigate these narrow, curved passages.
- **Magnetic navigation** steers flexible devices using a controlled magnetic field, connecting external robot hardware with an instrument inside the body.
- **Telerobotics** means operating a robot from another location; Nanoflex is developing remote intervention technology, including work on stroke treatment.

> **Key idea:** Robotics can control a flexible instrument through magnetic fields instead of moving a conventional rigid arm at the working tip.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a remote-control API:** commands, device state, and operator feedback must remain coordinated even when the person and mechanism are separated.
- **Worked example:** trace operator input to magnetic steering to observed tip movement; identify the feedback needed before choosing the next command.
- **A useful research distinction** is development evidence versus clinical readiness; the company’s transatlantic thrombectomy announcement explicitly describes an animal study.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official technology film** and locate the external magnetic system and the flexible instrument it guides.
2. **Read the technology and study pages** and draw the operator–controller–instrument feedback path; keep any student experiment entirely nonclinical.
3. **Use the public company contact** to ask about an educational discussion on flexible-device control or remote feedback, bringing your diagram and one focused question.

lessons.summary: Nature Robots develops autonomy software that helps agricultural machines localize, plan field work, follow rows, and respond to obstacles.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Nature Robots develops autonomy software that helps agricultural machines localize, plan field work, follow rows, and respond to obstacles.

![Nature Robots mission-control interface for planning agricultural robot work](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-nature-robots.webp)
*Nature Robots mission-control interface for planning agricultural robot work. Source: [Nature Robots](https://naturerobots.com/en/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Farming Autonomy Operating System** combines localization, route planning, motion control, obstacle perception, and remote operator oversight.
- **Localization** means estimating the machine’s position; Nature Robots combines laser sensing, stereo cameras, and motion sensors, with satellite positioning when available.
- **Coverage planning** chooses paths that work across a whole field, respecting boundaries, rows, obstacles, and space needed for turns.

> **Key idea:** Driving one row is only a small part of completing a reliable field mission.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a job scheduler with geometry:** the system must assign work and find physically drivable connections between the assigned regions.
- **Worked example:** inspect the mission-control demonstration; distinguish drawing a field boundary, assigning rows, and linking those rows into a mission.
- **Nature Robots Farming Autonomy OS** is the connected map node; compare its field workflow with general indoor navigation before reusing assumptions.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official machine and interface demonstrations** to identify where the operator supplies boundaries and task choices.
2. **Read the technology and product pages** and sketch how positioning failure or a newly detected obstacle should change the current mission.
3. **Check public Autonomy Days information** for educational discussions and demonstrations; confirm dates and participation conditions through the company’s public event channels.

Helsing develops defence AI software and autonomous systems, connecting sensing, decision support, and physical platforms.

![Helsing-published photograph of software being used in the field](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-helsing.webp)
*Helsing-published photograph of software being used in the field. Source: [Helsing](https://helsing.ai/company), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Defence AI** is software applied to military information and machines; Helsing works with governments and industrial partners on existing and new hardware.
- **Its public portfolio** spans information software, aircraft, and maritime systems; these are different products rather than a single general-purpose robot.
- **Human oversight** includes interface design: Helsing’s ethics page discusses how workload, fatigue, and perceived AI reliability affect a person’s ability to scrutinize results.

> **Key idea:** Putting a person in a decision loop requires interfaces and evidence that let that person understand and challenge the software.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an observability dashboard:** an output is useful only if the operator can interpret its context, uncertainty, and consequences.
- **Worked example:** compare a sensor observation with an interpretation shown on screen; list the provenance and confidence information a reviewer would need.
- **For 42AI,** the accessible learning opportunity is studying software–hardware integration and human oversight through public material, with civilian interface prototypes.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official introductory footage** and distinguish an information interface from a physical autonomous platform.
2. **Read the company’s ethics discussion** alongside the product descriptions; identify stated responsibilities and questions the public pages leave unanswered.
3. **Use public company or developer channels** for an educational conversation about explainability and evaluation; bring a clear, non-operational research question.

Loki Robotics builds cleaning robots that manipulate tools and fixtures in commercial restrooms, kitchens, and other changing indoor spaces.

*Loki Robotics official logo. Source: [Loki Robotics](https://lokirobotics.co/), license unknown.*

- **Manipulation** means physically handling objects; Loki describes changing tools, applying cleaning agents, and interacting with fixtures rather than only sweeping floors.

> **Key idea:** Cleaning requires coordinating movement, contact, and tool choice in spaces that were designed for people.

- **Think of a stateful workflow:** reaching a sink, selecting a tool, and scrubbing it have different prerequisites and failure conditions.
- **Worked example:** watch a cleaning sequence and separate navigation from contact; list what should happen if the tool misses the intended surface.
- **For 42AI,** this is a useful case study in learning a bounded job before claiming general-purpose capability across unrelated tasks.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official cleaning clips** and identify where the robot changes tools or makes contact with a fixture.
2. **Read the investor explanation and independent report** to compare the intended starting market with the longer-term autonomy ambition.

## In one sentence

Marso Robotics develops autonomous robots for repetitive warehouse work in existing buildings, with human supervision when needed.

![Marso Robotics official brand mark](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-marso-robotics.webp)
*Marso Robotics official brand mark. Source: [Marso Robotics](https://marsorobotics.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Brownfield deployment** means adding automation to a site already in use, rather than designing a new building around the robot.
- **The company targets** picking, sorting, packing, loading, and unloading goods; its official description emphasizes fitting the warehouse’s existing workflow.
- **Public coverage describes** onboard AI combined with human supervision for unexpected situations; STATION F selected Marso Robotics for its Future 40 in 2025.

> **Key idea:** A warehouse robot’s value depends on fitting the real operation, including the situations where automation needs help.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of integrating a service into a running application:** existing interfaces, timing, and exception paths matter as much as the new component.
- **Worked example:** compare taking an item from a container with sorting it to a destination; identify the observations and handover conditions each stage needs.
- **For 42AI,** the company offers a concrete French ecosystem example of applied logistics automation and the difference between a lab task and an operational service.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the public Marso interview** for the team’s explanation of its intralogistics approach; intralogistics means moving goods within a facility.
2. **Read the official task list** and sketch a small warehouse workflow, marking human handovers and recovery from an unrecognized item.
3. **Use the company’s published contact channel** with that sketch and one question about deployment constraints; consult STATION F’s public ecosystem material for context.

## In one sentence

microagi develops embodied AI through workplace data collection, model training, and robot deployment, organized around its Atlas platform.

*microagi’s published illustration of workplace data capture. Source: [microagi](https://www.microagi.ai/atlas), license unknown.*

- **Embodied AI** is intelligence acting through a physical system, where observations must eventually become useful movements.
- **Atlas (microagi)** is the connected map node; the company describes three layers: capturing manual work, training models, and deploying suitable robots.
- **Data capture:** shift by microagi is its recording product; the company emphasizes recording real work without teleoperation or interrupting the production line.

> **Key idea:** Workplace recordings become valuable when they connect to a task, an evaluation method, and a robot that can carry out the result.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an ML data pipeline:** raw recordings require useful structure before they become examples a model can learn from.
- **Worked example:** trace one assembly recording through Atlas’s three layers; distinguish observing a person from commanding a robot to repeat the action.
- **For 42AI,** this connects data engineering with deployment: an accurate offline model still needs a physical task and operational feedback.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official Atlas overview** and label the stages that collect data, change a model, or move a real machine.
2. **Read the Atlas and Shift explanations** and design a consent-based tabletop recording exercise with clear task boundaries and a separate evaluation set.
3. **Use the public contact route** to discuss dataset structure or evaluation, bringing an example annotation scheme rather than assuming access to proprietary models.

- **For 42AI,** this shows robotics outside walking and grasping: controlled instrument positioning, data quality, and understandable interfaces matter together.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official system footage** and identify the patient interface, measurement hardware, and report presentation.
2. **Read the product workflow** and draw a data-flow diagram using fictional records; mark where an incomplete measurement should be visible.

2. **Read the independent company profile** alongside Motion’s explanation; describe one narrow task and the evidence needed to assess whether a humanoid suits it.

## In one sentence

MS-Innov developed MORFOSE, a modular industrial robot whose programming software and replaceable joint modules support adaptable production equipment.

![Close view of MORFOSE’s industrial robot joint modules](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-ms-innov.webp)
*Close view of MORFOSE’s industrial robot joint modules. Source: [MS-Innov](https://european-robotics.fr/robot-morfose), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **MORFOSE** is the connected robot node; the current European Robotics product page credits MS-Innov with its control and programming software.
- **Modular construction** means the arm is assembled from replaceable units, allowing its configuration and maintenance to follow the production task.
- **The 2025 technical sheet** lists a six-axis arm: the short version carries eleven kilograms over 900 millimeters; the longer version carries five over 1,200 millimeters.

> **Key idea:** Changing a robot’s geometry changes which tasks it can reach and which loads it can handle.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a plugin architecture:** interchangeable components need agreed interfaces, but a different physical arrangement also changes the motion problem.
- **Worked example:** compare the short and long versions in the technical sheet; a farther target and a heavier object create different selection requirements.
- **For 42AI,** MORFOSE connects mechanisms with accessible programming; the machine-loading brochure shows how a robot becomes part of a complete production station.

## How to engage

1. **Watch MS-Innov’s assembly demonstration** and identify the modules and their mechanical connections.
2. **Read the dated technical sheet** before repeating specifications; its per-axis limits are more precise than the product page’s broad rotation claim.
3. **Use the current public product contact** at European Robotics for an educational modularity discussion, bringing a task sketch with reach and load requirements.

lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Mujin develops industrial robot-control software that connects perception, motion planning, and equipment coordination through its MujinOS platform.

![Mujin’s robot-cell interface displayed on a tablet](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-mujin.webp)
*Mujin’s robot-cell interface displayed on a tablet. Source: [Mujin](https://www.mujin-corp.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **MujinOS** is a control layer connecting robots, cameras, conveyors, and other production equipment through one configurable system.
- **Perception** estimates what is in the workspace; motion planning then chooses a path, and execution commands the connected machines.
- **A digital twin** is a software representation of the physical equipment; Mujin describes using it to validate motions before execution.

> **Key idea:** A successful pick depends on coordinating the whole workcell, not only calculating where the gripper should go.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an orchestration service:** the camera, arm, and conveyor provide different capabilities, and the controller must coordinate their timing and state.
- **Worked example:** follow bin picking from locating a loose part to moving it onto an output conveyor; separate observation, planning, and execution.
- **MujinController PickWorker and MujinOS** are connected map nodes; compare a specific picking system with the broader software platform that supports applications.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official automation footage** and identify the surrounding equipment that participates in each pick.
2. **Read the technology and bin-picking pages** and draw a message sequence for part detection, robot movement, and conveyor handover.
3. **Use public case studies or the company contact** to explore integration questions, bringing your sequence diagram and one clearly defined exception such as an empty bin.

lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Naiture develops BEAM, an agricultural robot that uses camera-based plant recognition and targeted lasers to remove weeds without chemical herbicides.

![Naiture BEAM laser-weeding equipment working in a field](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_3-naiture.webp)
*Naiture BEAM laser-weeding equipment working in a field. Source: [Naiture](https://naiture.org), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Weed recognition** separates unwanted plants from the crop using camera images; the company trains a visual neural network for this classification task.
- **BEAM** combines cameras, lighting, scanners, and laser units; the published modular design supports working widths from three to six meters.
- **Targeted treatment** directs laser energy at detected weeds; Naiture’s approach connects image interpretation to a physical action on a living plant.

> **Key idea:** Classification accuracy matters because a perception error can directly damage the crop instead of only producing a wrong label.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a spam filter with physical output:** a false positive means the system acts on something it should have kept.
- **Worked example:** take one field image, mark crop and weed locations, then separately review missed weeds and crops incorrectly selected for treatment.
- **Naiture laser weeding robot** is the connected map node; use its field setting to study lighting changes, plant variation, and the timing between detection and treatment.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official field clips** to connect the wide agricultural machine with the small plants it must recognize.
2. **Read the regional report and company updates** before designing an offline image-labeling exercise; evaluate crop preservation separately from weed detection.
3. **Use the public company contact** for a field-perception discussion, bringing annotated images and questions about data collection.
